svg.aria-label: Soma milestone roadmap from M0 architecture convergence through independent M1a, M1b and M1c checkpoints to hardware and fleet milestones, showing what triggers each one
svg.text: Milestones — and what opens each one
Only M0 and M1 are current scope. Later milestones are designed but closed; each names the trigger that reopens it, so scope cannot drift in by ambition.

g.text: Exit — one meaning per term for Plant, timeline, generation, capability, and safety authority. Every P0 decision is accepted, provisional with a reversal trigger, or assigned an experiment.
Produces the Decision Register, the threat model, the verification matrix, and the Performance Envelope template.
Gate — Python acquires a lease and commands MuJoCo through separate robot-runtime and robot-rt processes. Reset issues a new Plant timeline and refuses the stale command.
Command lineage stays visible end to end. The first executable proof that the architecture is a system and not a vocabulary.
Gate — runtime recovery, bounded IPC negatives, and a representative-board 24-hour end-to-end qualification that sets the final IPC budget.
Plus vendor-neutral adapter conformance, systemd supervision, and an installable Linux x86_64 candidate.
Gate — live recorder pressure is bounded, Copper adoption is decided against the native graph, and stateful replay passes its declared negative cases.
May explicitly defer stateful replay and retain message-level replay only; that result does not reopen M1a or M1b.
Trigger — hardware becomes accessible and a real need justifies it. Classify the boundary as a NativePlantAdapter or a ManagedMotionGateway, then rerun the M1 scenarios.
A managed vendor motion boundary never inherits Soma SA-3 coverage. Inaccessible layers are published as unknown, not inferred.
Trigger — Soma owns hardware or an accessible bench. Constrained single actuator, then a synchronized multi-axis fixture, with firmware and HAL owned for every claimed layer.
Independent stop or energy-control path chosen by hazard analysis. Must not require rewriting the M1 public contracts.
Trigger — something exists that is worth shipping. Provisioning, signing roles, secure boot, anti-rollback, recovery; abuse and fuzz qualification; canary rollout and rollback.
M1 remains loopback-only local development: no cryptographic mechanism is implemented or security-qualified.

svg.text: EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE FOR MILESTONE 1
Physical robot, fieldbus, E-stop, STO, hard-real-time actuation qualification · a universal URDF/MJCF/USD compiler · complete vendor emulators
Non-local security, cryptographic trust/update mechanisms · Isaac, Genesis, batch-RL infrastructure, ROS distributions · aarch64 before target selection
Fleet rollout, cloud services and UI tooling · plugin ABI and cross-version internal IPC compatibility · any safety-certification claim
These items reopen only at their named hardware, policy, security, target or product trigger.
